messages:
maya: Heads-up: got a customer ticket reporting a sudden spike in 429s right after yesterday's rate policy push. They say it started ~09:12 UTC and is impacting batch embedding jobs.

maya: Metrics: spike in per-key 429 rate from ~0.3% to 18% between 09:12-09:20. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rate/429s?orgId=1 (private)

jason: thanks — which policy was deployed? I think the staged rollout pushed policy v2 (tightened per-second limits) at 09:10 with 20% canary.

maya: correct, policy v2: reduced burst allowance for free-tier keys. Some affected keys are enterprise too though (weird).

alex: can we get a quick repro and logs? ask customer for an example request-id or API key. Also check edge auth logs for 401/403 vs 429.

maya: customer provided request-id: req_0a7c9f. Sample curl they used:
```
curl -X POST \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-XXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-001","input":["a","b","c"]}'
```
Response they saw: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{ "error": "rate limit exceeded", "retry_after": 10 }

jason: checking canary logs now. If v2 was at 20% bucket, maybe our routing sent them to canary accidentally due to upstream sticky routing.

deploy-bot: policy-rollout v2 -> status: deployed @ 2024-10-12T09:10:12Z (canary 20%) :rocket:

alex: I see that key sk-customer-XXX is in the enterprise tier; it should've been on dedicated limits. Need to verify customer tagging service. Possible tag propagation delay caused them to be treated as free-tier during rollout.

jason: good call. Also saw a small bug in the rollout script: when tag-service returns 503, fallback path uses default (free-tier) limits. There's a race during canary where tag-service was redeployed.

maya: ops: customer is upset, asking for rollback and ETA. Can we roll back the canary quickly and then do a fix + re-deploy?

alex: I can roll back the policy for the canary slice. Command I'll run:
```
infractl rate-policy rollback --policy v2 --canary-slice 20 --to v1
```
I'll also disable routing sticky for edge nodes temporarily.

jason: before rollback, let's ensure no other customers are seeing elevated 429s. Quick check: run query across last 30m for keys with >5% 429.

alex: ran it: only 3 keys breached threshold, including sk-customer-XXX. Others are transient. OK proceeding with rollback.

deploy-bot: rollback started for policy v2 canary slice at 2024-10-12T09:23:01Z.

deploy-bot: rollback complete at 2024-10-12T09:23:42Z. Changes: canary slice reverted to v1 behavior.

maya: customer confirmed 429s dropped to baseline within ~90s after rollback. :thumbsup:

jason: root cause follow-up: rollout script should treat tag-service errors as 'retry' not 'fallback to default'. I'll file a PR to add stronger health-check gating and increase canary warm-up delay.

alex: also adding a short circuit in routing: if a key's tier is unknown, route to safe/v1 until resolved. That should prevent regressions.

maya: noted. Customer wants postmortem and a timeline for the fix and redeploy. I'll draft a summary and ping them.

jason: ETA for fix + redeploy: I can open PR now, test in staging, and aim for re-deploy next Tue with a 5% canary and longer observation window.

alex: I'll update the runbook steps for policy rollouts to include explicit tag-service dependency check and a preflight that simulates missing tags.

maya: thanks team. Closing ticket after PM updates and runbook linked.

maya: quick notes for the postmortem:
- timeline: v2 canary deploy @ 09:10, 429s spike @ 09:12, rollback @ 09:23, resolved @ 09:25.
- impact: customer embedding jobs failed for ~13 minutes, 2 other minor transient keys briefly affected.
- root cause: tag-service 503 during canary -> rollout fallback treated keys as free-tier.
- immediate fix: rollback + routing safe-path.
- long-term: change fallback behavior, add gating and preflight tests.

alex: adding to /runbooks/policy-rollouts.md and will PR for review.

jason: adding a monitoring alert for tag-service error rates crossing 1% during rollouts.

maya: great. I'll update customer and mark as resolved once postmortem is shared.
